newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW-German inflation data, import prices.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-German inflation data, import prices.

text.p: Economists made the following comments on Tuesday on Reuters Financial Television about two German state February inflation reports and German January import prices.
January import prices rose 1.0 percent from December and were up 2.6 percent year-on-year, with the sharp dollar rise being seen behind the price increase.

The state of Hesse said February consumer prices gained 0.3 percent month-on-month for a year-on-year rate of 1.5 percent. The state of Baden-Wuerttemberg said February prices rose 0.4 percent and 1.7 percent year-on-year.
"I would say they were satisfying. It (the CPI rise) was very much expected."

Regarding import prices, Beckmann said, "We know what the effects are, mainly the rise of the dollar against the mark and the colder weather. Import prices are feeding through rapidly into Germany, and they have been incorporated into the negative CPI figures for January.

"We do not expect the mark to weaken substantially in the coming months. We see it around 1.70 marks. I still see the chance for the dollar...(to)..go to 1.75 marks for a short time. Every 10-percent increase in (the) dollar is a 0.2-percent increase in consumer prices.
"The Bund market developments will depend very much on the United States. However, if we do see rates rising due to a Fed hike in the next few months, there could be a setback in the German market."
"The inflation figures for February are a little low for the time of the year."
Regarding the dollar, Schroeder said, "I think only the mark over two marks to the dollar will cause some fears that we would see a flare up in import prices."
"The overall price picture remains very moderate. What we see here is that weak domestic demand makes it difficult for corporations to pass on price hikes. We see that continuing for the time being.
"I see no reason why inflation should pick up. There is a possibility we could get some positive surprises on inflation rates in the next two months.
"Oil prices declined more than 20 percent in a four-week period. That is a significant event and should help consumer prices.
"We have had some profit-taking in the dollar but in the end, the fundamental picture has not changed. The upward trend is still intact."
